AMy Initial Understanding

Do teenagers manage money and internet behavior wisely?

Infografis pembuka: personal money management, needs vs wants, saving, budget, dan spending habits.

Situational Hook

Bayangkan situasi berikut. Kamu tinggal di wilayah kepulauan. Banyak kebutuhan harus dibeli dari luar pulau atau menunggu kapal datang. Kadang harga barang naik karena biaya pengiriman. Di sisi lain, internet membuat belanja online, game online, paket data, dan gaya hidup digital semakin mudah diakses. Sebagian siswa mulai sulit membedakan needs dan wants.

At the same time, students also communicate online every day. They comment on posts, join class groups, send messages, and share information. Without good netiquette, online communication can become rude, harmful, or misleading.

BConcept Exploration

What is Hortatory Exposition Text?

Hortatory exposition text is a text that presents the writer’s opinion about an issue, supports it with arguments, and ends with a recommendation that tells readers what they should do or avoid.

Artinya: Hortatory exposition text adalah teks yang menyampaikan pendapat penulis tentang suatu isu, mendukungnya dengan argumen, lalu diakhiri dengan rekomendasi tindakan yang sebaiknya dilakukan atau dihindari pembaca.

Social Function

The social function of hortatory exposition text is to persuade readers or listeners to take action, change behavior, or avoid a harmful action.

Text Structure

StructureFunctionGuiding QuestionExample
ThesisStates the issue and writer’s positionWhat does the writer believe?Teenagers should manage their money wisely.
ArgumentsGives reasons and evidenceWhy should readers agree?First, saving money builds responsibility.
RecommendationSuggests actionWhat should readers do?Therefore, students should make a weekly budget and save regularly.

Analytical Exposition vs Hortatory Exposition

AspectAnalytical ExpositionHortatory Exposition
PurposeTo persuade readers that an issue is important or trueTo persuade readers to do or avoid something
EndingReiterationRecommendation
Final messageRestates writer’s positionGives suggested action
Example thesisDigital literacy is essential for students.Students should practice netiquette in every online interaction.
Example endingTherefore, digital literacy is important.Therefore, students must check their words before posting online.

Language Features

Simple Present TenseModal AuxiliariesAbstract NounsPassive VoiceCausal ConnectorsPersuasive ExpressionsRecommendation Language

Infografis pendukung Reading Text 1: netiquette, privacy, polite language, and checking information.

Reading Text 1: Students Should Practice Netiquette in Online Communication

[Thesis] Students should practice netiquette in every online communication. Today, students use messaging applications, social media, learning platforms, and online discussion groups almost every day. These digital spaces are useful for learning and communication. However, without good manners, online interaction can easily become rude, careless, or harmful.

[Argument 1] First, netiquette protects people from emotional harm. A short comment may look simple, but it can hurt someone’s feelings when it is written harshly. Some students may make jokes about their friends’ appearance, mistakes, or family background without thinking about the impact. This behavior is dangerous because online words can be saved, shared, and remembered for a long time. Therefore, students should think carefully before sending messages or posting comments.

[Argument 2] Second, netiquette helps students build responsible digital identity. What students write online can influence how others see them. Rude language, false information, and disrespectful comments can damage a student’s reputation. On the other hand, polite responses, useful information, and respectful discussion can show maturity and responsibility. In the digital world, character is also shown through words and actions online.

[Argument 3] Third, netiquette supports better learning communication. In class groups, students often ask questions, share assignments, or discuss school activities. If communication is unclear or impolite, misunderstanding may happen. For example, students may ignore instructions, send messages at inappropriate times, or use informal language when contacting teachers. Clear and respectful communication makes learning more organized and comfortable.

[Recommendation] For these reasons, students must practice netiquette seriously. Before posting or sending messages, students should ask themselves: Is it true? Is it kind? Is it necessary? Schools should also remind students to use polite language, check information before sharing it, and respect others in every online space.

Reading Text 2: Teenagers Should Start Saving Money Early

[Thesis] Teenagers should start saving money early because financial habits are built through repeated small actions. Many students receive allowance from their parents, earn small income from helping family businesses, or get money during special events. If this money is always spent without planning, students may develop careless financial habits. Therefore, saving money should become part of teenagers’ daily discipline.

[Argument 1] First, saving money teaches responsibility. Students learn that money is limited and should be used wisely. In island communities, some goods may be more expensive because they need to be transported by boat. This condition shows that money management is important. When students learn to separate needs from wants, they become more responsible in making decisions.

[Argument 2] Second, saving money helps students prepare for unexpected needs. A student may suddenly need money for school supplies, internet data for learning, transportation, or family emergencies. Without savings, students may depend completely on their parents or borrow money from friends. Savings may not solve every problem, but they can reduce stress when urgent needs appear.

[Argument 3] Third, saving money can protect teenagers from unhealthy financial behavior. Online shopping promotions, game items, snacks, and social media trends can encourage students to spend quickly. Some young people may even borrow money for things they do not really need. This habit is risky because small debts can become bigger problems when they are ignored.

[Recommendation] For these reasons, teenagers should start saving money early. Students ought to make a simple budget, separate needs and wants, save a small amount regularly, and avoid borrowing money for unnecessary items. Schools and families should also teach personal money management so that young people can build financial discipline from an early age.

DListening Section

Radio Interview: Avoiding Debt and Planning the Future

Listening context: radio interview about avoiding debt and planning future financial choices.

Pre-Listening Activity

  1. What do teenagers usually borrow money for?
  2. Why can small debts become a problem?
  3. What is better: buying something immediately or saving first?
  4. How can young people prepare for the future?

Natural TTS Browser Mode

Pilih suara English terbaik yang tersedia di browser/perangkat. Kalimat yang sedang dibaca akan ter-highlight. Klik kalimat mana pun untuk replay.

Status: ready
Click Play Full or click any sentence below.

Host: Good afternoon, listeners. Welcome to Youth Voice Radio. Today, we are talking about smart money choices for teenagers. Our guest is Ms. Lina, a community educator who works with young people. Welcome, Ms. Lina.

Guest: Thank you. I am happy to be here.

Host: Many teenagers today spend money on snacks, internet data, online shopping, and game items. Some even borrow money from friends. Why should teenagers be careful with debt?

Guest: Teenagers should be careful with debt because borrowing money can become a habit. At first, the amount may seem small. However, when students borrow again and again, the debt becomes difficult to control. Debt should not be used for unnecessary items such as trends, game items, or impulse shopping.

Host: That is an important point. What should students do when they want to buy something?

Guest: They should pause and ask three questions. First, do I really need this item? Second, can I afford it without borrowing? Third, will this item still be useful next week or next month? These questions help students separate needs from wants.

Host: Some students say that saving money is difficult because their allowance is small. What do you think?

Guest: Saving does not always start with a large amount. It can start with a small and regular habit. For example, students can save a little money every week. The amount is not the most important thing. The habit is more important. Financial discipline is built through consistency.

Host: What about students in island areas where transportation and goods may be more expensive?

Guest: That is exactly why money management is important. When transportation costs are higher, students and families need to plan spending more carefully. Students should not waste money on things they do not need. Instead, they ought to prepare for school needs, internet data for learning, transportation, or emergencies.

Host: What final recommendation would you give to teenagers?

Guest: Teenagers must learn to manage money early. They should make a simple budget, save regularly, avoid unnecessary debt, and discuss financial decisions with parents or trusted adults. Good money habits today can help them prepare for a better future.

Host: Thank you, Ms. Lina. That was very useful. Listeners, remember: small choices today can shape your future.

E.1 Abstract Nouns

Abstract nouns are nouns that refer to ideas, qualities, feelings, or concepts that cannot be touched physically. Artinya: kata benda yang merujuk pada gagasan, kualitas, perasaan, atau konsep yang tidak dapat disentuh secara fisik.

E.2 Modal Auxiliaries: Should, Must, Ought To

Modal auxiliaries are used to express recommendation, obligation, advice, or necessity. Artinya: digunakan untuk menyatakan saran, kewajiban, nasihat, atau keharusan.

ModalStrengthMeaningExampleArti
shouldadvice/recommendationsebaiknyaStudents should save regularly.Siswa sebaiknya menabung secara teratur.
ought tostrong advice/moral recommendationsepatutnya/sebaiknyaTeenagers ought to avoid unnecessary debt.Remaja sepatutnya menghindari utang yang tidak perlu.
muststrong obligation/necessityharusStudents must respect others online.Siswa harus menghargai orang lain secara online.
must notprohibitiontidak bolehStudents must not share private information carelessly.Siswa tidak boleh membagikan informasi pribadi sembarangan.

Pattern

PatternExample
Subject + should + V1Students should make a simple budget.
Subject + must + V1Students must practice netiquette.
Subject + ought to + V1Teenagers ought to save part of their allowance.
Subject + must not + V1Students must not write harmful comments.

Common Mistakes

IncorrectCorrectExplanation
Students should to save money.Students should save money.After modal, use V1 without “to”.
Teenagers must saves money.Teenagers must save money.After modal, use base verb.
Students ought save regularly.Students ought to save regularly.Use “ought to”.
We must not to share private data.We must not share private data.After must not, use V1.
Students should saving money.Students should save money.Use base verb after modal.

E.3 Passive Voice

Passive voice focuses on the action or the object receiving the action, not the person doing it. Artinya: kalimat pasif menekankan tindakan atau objek yang menerima tindakan, bukan pelakunya.

Tense / FormPatternExampleArti
Simple Present Passiveis/am/are + V3Online messages are written every day.Pesan online ditulis setiap hari.
Modal Passivemodal + be + V3Private information must be protected.Informasi pribadi harus dilindungi.
Recommendation Passiveshould be + V3Money should be managed wisely.Uang sebaiknya dikelola dengan bijak.

Passive Voice in Hortatory Exposition

Active SentencePassive SentenceArti Passive

Students must check information.Information must be checked.Informasi harus diperiksa.
Teenagers should manage money wisely.Money should be managed wisely.Uang sebaiknya dikelola dengan bijak.
Schools should teach financial literacy.Financial literacy should be taught at school.Literasi keuangan sebaiknya diajarkan di sekolah.
Students must avoid unnecessary debt.Unnecessary debt must be avoided.Utang yang tidak perlu harus dihindari.

Writing Structure

ParagraphContent

Paragraph 4Argument 3: third reason and evidence

Thesis Builder

[Group] should / must / ought to [action] because [reason 1], [reason 2], and [reason 3].
  1. Teenagers should start saving money early because it builds responsibility, prepares them for unexpected needs, and protects them from unnecessary debt.
    Remaja sebaiknya mulai menabung sejak dini karena hal itu membangun tanggung jawab, mempersiapkan mereka menghadapi kebutuhan tak terduga, dan melindungi mereka dari utang yang tidak perlu.
  2. Students must practice netiquette because online words can hurt others, shape digital identity, and affect learning communication.
  3. Schools should teach personal money management because many teenagers need guidance in budgeting, saving, and avoiding impulse buying.

Recommendation Builder

PatternExample
Therefore, students should...Therefore, students should save a small amount every week.
For these reasons, teenagers must...For these reasons, teenagers must avoid borrowing money for trends.
Schools should encourage students to...Schools should encourage students to discuss money management.
It is recommended that...It is recommended that students make a simple budget.
Young people ought to...Young people ought to separate needs from wants.

Model Text A: Reader’s Letter — Dear School Magazine, Students Should Learn Personal Money Management

Dear School Magazine,

I strongly believe that students should learn personal money management at school. Many teenagers receive allowance, but not all of them know how to use it wisely. Some students spend money quickly on snacks, online shopping, game items, or trends. This habit can become a serious problem if it is not guided.

First, money management teaches responsibility. Students need to understand that money is limited. If they spend all their allowance without planning, they may not have money for important school needs. By learning how to make a simple budget, students can separate needs from wants.

Second, money management helps students prepare for unexpected needs. In island areas, students may need money for transportation, internet data, or school supplies. Sometimes, families also face sudden needs. Small savings can help students reduce stress when unexpected situations happen.

Third, money management can prevent unnecessary debt. Some teenagers borrow money from friends to buy things they do not really need. This habit is risky because debt can grow when it is ignored. Students should not borrow money only to follow trends.

Therefore, schools should teach personal money management through simple and practical activities. Students should be encouraged to make a weekly budget, save regularly, and discuss financial choices with parents or trusted adults. Good financial habits should be built early.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student

FeatureExample

Argument 3Money management can prevent unnecessary debt.
RecommendationSchools should teach personal money management...
Modal auxiliariesshould, can
Abstract nounsresponsibility, management, savings
Passive voiceGood financial habits should be built early.

Model Text B: Opinion Article — Students Must Practice Netiquette in Every Online Space

Students must practice netiquette in every online space because digital communication is now part of daily student life. Class groups, social media comments, and learning platforms can support communication, but they can also become harmful when students use them carelessly.

First, netiquette protects people from emotional harm. A rude comment may be written in only a few seconds, but its impact can last much longer. Online words can be saved, shared, and misunderstood. Therefore, students must think before they post.

Second, netiquette helps students build a positive digital identity. What students write online can show their character. Polite language, useful information, and respectful replies show maturity. On the other hand, harmful posts and rude comments can damage reputation.

Third, netiquette supports better school communication. In class groups, students often receive instructions, ask questions, and share learning materials. Messages should be written clearly and politely so that misunderstanding can be avoided.

For these reasons, students must practice netiquette seriously. They should use polite language, respect privacy, check information before sharing it, and avoid harmful comments. Schools should also create clear guidelines for online communication so that digital spaces can become safer and more useful for learning.

Sample Persuasive Speech: Start Saving Money This Week

Good morning, everyone.

Today, I would like to talk about why students should start saving money this week. Many of us receive allowance from our parents. Some of us also get money during special events or from helping our families. However, if we spend all of our money without planning, we may develop careless financial habits.

First, saving money teaches responsibility. When we save even a small amount, we learn that money should be managed wisely. We also learn to separate needs from wants.

Second, saving money helps us prepare for unexpected needs. Sometimes we need money for school supplies, internet data, transportation, or family emergencies. Small savings can help us face these situations more calmly.

Third, saving money can protect us from unnecessary debt. We should not borrow money only to follow trends, buy game items, or join online shopping promotions. Debt may look small at first, but it can become a serious problem if it is repeated.

Therefore, I invite all of us to start saving money this week. We should make a simple budget, save a small amount regularly, and avoid buying unnecessary items. Small choices today can build a better future.

Thank you.
